intent: Name a form control so the name is announced to assistive tech and clicking the caption drives the control.
typical_uses: A caption naming one control, associated with it via htmlFor
An inline caption wrapped around a checkbox or a switch, where the label itself is the click target

dont_use_when.situation: Headings and free-standing text that name no control

instead.target: the consuming application's own text markup (a heading or paragraph element)
instead.note: The kit ships no generic text component, and a label with no control attached contributes nothing to assistive tech: a caption belongs to a control.

dont_use_when.situation: A caption inside a Field composition

instead.note: FieldLabel is this Label with Field's spacing, and Field's own data-disabled dims it; the htmlFor association is still wired by hand.

invariants.text: The component adds no association of its own: a Label with neither htmlFor nor a nested control names nothing. Both accepted forms - htmlFor pointing at the control's id, and the control nested inside - produce the same native association, and either one makes the caption the control's click target.

A data-disabled attribute dims the label to the controls' own disabled opacity and stops pointer events. Nothing sets it automatically: a consumer sets it by hand. Inside a Field, Field's own data-disabled dims FieldLabel instead.
The label declares no color of its own: it inherits from its context, so a Field carrying data-invalid tints the caption destructive.

anti_patterns.dont: Render a label with no control associated with it
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass htmlFor pointing at the control's id, or nest the control inside the label

anti_patterns.dont: Let an input's placeholder stand in for a name
anti_patterns.do_instead: Caption the control with Label and keep the placeholder for an example value

a11y.by: label.test.tsx - getByLabelText finds the control associated via htmlFor, and a className merge with a data-disabled attribute is asserted on the rendered label

good.title: Associate a caption with its control
Inline caption as the control's click target

bad.title: An orphan label
bad.why: Neither htmlFor nor a nested control associates it with anything, so assistive tech gets no name and clicking it activates nothing. Pass htmlFor, or nest the control.

bad.title: A caption prop the component does not have
bad.why: Label forwards the native label attributes and declares none of its own - there is no text prop. The caption is children.
